nodes.authority: anyone (subject to the position being underwater at the mark)

The caller becomes the keeper at `msg` (PerpEngine.sol:943) and receives the keeper cut plus a badge.

nodes.name: sweepLiquidations
nodes.reachability: The keeperless liquidation entrypoint: the hook calls it from afterSwap on every trade on any interface, passing the swapper as `liquidator` (PerpEngine.sol:957). It runs with `inLocked` true, so settlement swaps execute in place inside the pool manager's existing lock rather than opening a new one. It carries no reentrancy modifier of its own - nesting is prevented by `_liqReentry` (PerpEngine.sol:981) inside the sweep. The hook discards the result, so anything that reverts in here rolls back every kill in the call. DERIVED.

observations: comment at `selfSweep` (PerpEngine.sol:964) documents this as the engine calling itself; the guard at `OnlyHook` (PerpEngine.sol:965) tests `address(this)` but reverts with the hook-named error.

nodes.name: _sweepAfterOpen
nodes.reachability: Best-effort cascade after an open. It refuses to start below a `g` (PerpEngine.sol:972) floor of 250k, forwards all but a 120k reserve at `fwd` (PerpEngine.sol:973), and swallows every failure in the empty catch at `catch` (PerpEngine.sol:974) so a liquidation cascade can never revert the trader's own open.

nodes.name: _doSweep
nodes.reachability: The bounded rotating scan. It pokes the oracle BEFORE the empty-book early return at `_pokeFunding` (PerpEngine.sol:992), so an idle pool still records observations. The loop is bounded three ways - `SWEEP_SCAN` (PerpEngine.sol:1000) checks, `MAX_LIQ_PER_SWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:1000) kills, and a gas floor of `SWEEP_KILL_RESERVE` (PerpEngine.sol:1016) that BREAKS rather than reverting. The cursor does not advance after a kill because `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1024) swap-popped a new occupant into the same slot; it is persisted at `sweepCursor` (PerpEngine.sol:1027) so coverage rotates across swaps. While it runs, `_inLocked` (PerpEngine.sol:996) makes every settlement swap run in place and `notNested` (PerpEngine.sol:505) locks out every user entrypoint.

nodes.name: _tryLiquidate
nodes.value: pays the keeper and trader through `_settle` (line 1048)
nodes.reachability: Identical checks to the keeper entrypoint but SILENT: a closed id, a healthy position or a full per-timestamp cap all `return` (PerpEngine.sol:1046) instead of reverting, which is what lets the surrounding sweep keep scanning. It assumes its caller already raised `_liqReentry` (PerpEngine.sol:995) and poked funding.

nodes.name: forceCloseDead
nodes.signature: function forceCloseDead(uint256 id) external nonReentrant notNested
nodes.value: pays the keeper and trader through `_settle` (line 1062)
nodes.reachability: Per-position death clearing. No penalty is taken in `MODE_DEATH` (PerpEngine.sol:1062); the caller earns only the keeper share of the residual computed at `reward` (PerpEngine.sol:1363). Death is EITHER the hook reporting the pool dead OR the cached quote diverging from the registry's, both decided by `_isDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1460).

nodes.name: forceCloseAllDead
nodes.authority: anyone (once the generation is dead); driven by the hook at relaunch
nodes.value: pays the keeper and every trader through `_settle` (line 1084)
nodes.reachability: Drains the whole book so nothing is trapped across a relaunch. It repeatedly settles `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1083) index 0, relying on the swap-and-pop in `_removeOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:1486) to refill that slot; the order is therefore deterministic and caller-independent. The loop bound `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:1082) is 96 while the book is capped at `MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS` (PerpEngine.sol:1477) of 64, which is what makes one call always sufficient. Called best-effort inside a try/catch by the hook at `forceCloseAllDead` (CauldronHook.sol:1848).
observations: comment at `Bounded` (PerpEngine.sol:1067) says the call is bounded to 64 positions; the loop at `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:1082) bounds it by the constant declared as 96 at `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:164).

nodes.name: syncGeneration
nodes.value: on a quote flip it sweeps the summed `plv`, `tokYieldEth` and `insuranceEth` (line 1218) to the treasury through `_tryPush` (line 1228), in the OLD asset, before `quote` (line 1245) is reassigned
nodes.reachability: The only place the engine adopts a generation or a quote, and now the only place a QUOTE ROTATION can be followed: the refusal at `syncedGeneration` (PerpEngine.sol:1109) is conditional on the quote too, so a rotation that leaves the generation unchanged is still syncable. Reached permissionlessly and also from the relaunch path, where it is wrapped in a try/catch. On a quote flip it demands `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1207) be zero and the vault report no stakers at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1208), then zeroes the three quote-denominated counters at `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1219), drops the mark source at `markSource` (PerpEngine.sol:1241) and re-reads the decimals at `quoteUnit` (PerpEngine.sol:1243). Every unmigrated token is recorded against its own token at `strandedToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1135) rather than silently overwritten.
observations: The second positions check at `openCount` (PerpEngine.sol:1163) is unreachable as a revert: the same condition already reverted at `openCount` (PerpEngine.sol:1110), which the comment above it acknowledges as a belt on that brace. DERIVED.

`ringArmedAt` (PerpEngine.sol:1148) is stamped here only; the constructor seeds `lastObsTs` (PerpEngine.sol:487) and `lastRingTs` (PerpEngine.sol:488) but not this, so on an engine that has never synced the ring warm-up term in the open guard starts from zero. DERIVED.

The sweep at `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1228) discards its result, so a treasury that cannot accept the old asset leaves the swept value in the engine as residue owned by nobody while the counters are already zero. DERIVED.

In-comment line pointers in this function are stale relative to the current file: the note at `_pushQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:1166) cites :1553 and `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1171) cites :1473, while those functions are declared at 213 and 1743.

nodes.name: isLiquidatable
nodes.signature: function isLiquidatable(uint256 id) external view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Frontend and keeper probe for the liquidation trigger; false for a closed id at `trader` (PerpEngine.sol:1255). It uses the same mark as the real check, so it is exact rather than advisory.

nodes.name: _underwater
nodes.signature: function _underwater(Position memory p) internal view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Convenience wrapper that computes the mark value itself; the hot liquidation paths deliberately call `_underwaterVal` (PerpEngine.sol:1269) directly so the ring is only walked once per kill.

nodes.name: _underwaterVal
nodes.signature: function _underwaterVal(Position memory p, uint256 val) internal view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: The solvency predicate, in two shapes. LONG: the token held is underwater when its mark value is below debt plus the maintenance buffer at `principal` (PerpEngine.sol:1272) - note collateral does not appear, because a long's collateral was already spent into the position. SHORT: underwater when the mark cost of buying back the owed size plus the buffer exceeds `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1277), where backing is collateral plus the proceeds held at `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1275).

nodes.name: _settle
nodes.signature: function _settle(uint256 id, Position memory p, uint256 minOut, uint8 mode, address keeper) internal
nodes.value: pays the keeper through `_payOut` (line 1350) and the trader through `_payOut` (line 1366)
nodes.reachability: The single exit for every position, in four stages. (1) Effects first: the position is deleted at `positions` (PerpEngine.sol:1282), removed from the enumerable set and `openCount` (PerpEngine.sol:1284) decremented, all before any swap. (2) Leg unwind - a LONG returns `longOiEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1289), sells its token, credits `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1293) with at most the principal and tops the gap up from insurance via `_replenishPlv` (PerpEngine.sol:1298); a SHORT buys back EXACTLY the borrowed size at `_buyExactOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1305), restores `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1306) in full, and any overspend beyond the position's backing is socialised through `_absorbPlvLoss` (PerpEngine.sol:1311). (3) Funding transfer: a payer is capped by its own residual at `residual` (PerpEngine.sol:1332), while a receiver draws insurance first and only then `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1339), saturating so neither can overdraw. (4) Mode tail - liquidation takes `liqPenaltyBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1345) of collateral capped by residual, splits off `keeperBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1347) and routes the rest as a fee; death mode instead pays `reward` (PerpEngine.sol:1363) to the caller. Slippage is enforced only when `ownerSlippage` (PerpEngine.sol:1286) is set, i.e. only on the trader's own close.
observations: comment at `PerpOps` (PerpEngine.sol:1317) says the settlement tail was extracted to a separate library for size headroom; the code computes it inline starting at `_fundingDelta` (PerpEngine.sol:1329), and no such library exists in this cluster.

nodes.name: _run
nodes.signature: function _run(SwapReq memory r) internal returns (bytes memory)
nodes.reachability: The lock-aware dispatcher. When `_inLocked` (PerpEngine.sol:1380) is set - i.e. we are inside the hook's afterSwap - it calls the swap body directly, because re-entering `unlock` (PerpEngine.sol:1380) would revert; otherwise it opens a fresh lock and the manager calls back into `unlockCallback` (PerpEngine.sol:1393). The fresh-lock branch calls `unlock` (PerpEngine.sol:1380) on the pool manager, which reenters this contract through the callback.

nodes.name: _swapExactIn
nodes.signature: function _swapExactIn(bool buy, uint256 amount) internal returns (uint256 out)
nodes.reachability: Exact-input leg. buy=true spends quote for token (opens a long, pushes price up); buy=false sells token for quote (opens a short or closes a long, pushes price down). Callers: `_swapExactIn` (PerpEngine.sol:875), `_swapExactIn` (PerpEngine.sol:911) and `_swapExactIn` (PerpEngine.sol:1290).

nodes.name: _buyExactOut
nodes.reachability: Exact-OUTPUT buy, used once: `_buyExactOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1305) makes the short inventory whole by acquiring exactly the borrowed size whatever it costs. That is the leg that can overspend a position's backing and therefore the only source of short-side bad debt.

nodes.name: unlockCallback
nodes.signature: function unlockCallback(bytes calldata raw) external returns (bytes memory)
nodes.reachability: Reachable only as the callback of an `unlock` (PerpEngine.sol:1380) the engine itself opened. The guard compares against the immutable `poolManager` (PerpEngine.sol:1394); note that it reverts with the trader-named error rather than a dedicated one. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _swapBody
nodes.signature: function _swapBody(SwapReq memory r) internal returns (bytes memory)
nodes.reachability: Decides which pool currency is the quote by comparing currency1 against `syncedToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1410) - derived from the engine's own armed token rather than stored, so the engine and the library cannot disagree about leg orientation. Gacha volume from perp swaps is attributed by encoding `nftBeneficiary` (PerpEngine.sol:1419) as hook data. The return encoding differs by request shape: an exact-out buy returns spend, everything else returns receipt (`spent` (PerpEngine.sol:1421)).

nodes.name: _guardOpen
nodes.reachability: The single gate both open paths pass, at `_guardOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:856) and `_guardOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:893). It now takes the LATER of two warm-ups — the summon clock at `warmup` (PerpEngine.sol:1435) and the observation-ring clock at `ringWarm` (PerpEngine.sol:1436), stamped when a sync wipes the ring — so opens are refused until the ring genuinely spans `twapWindow` (PerpEngine.sol:1436) again, not merely the MIN_TWAP its fallback will trust. It then refuses a dead or quote-diverged pool at `_isDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1438) and caps leverage at `maxLeverage` (PerpEngine.sol:1439).
observations: The ring gate binds only after a sync has stamped `ringArmedAt` (PerpEngine.sol:1148); before that it is `0 + twapWindow` and the summon clock is what holds, because the constructor does not stamp it. DERIVED.
Only OPENS are gated. Liquidations, closes and the in-swap sweep never call this, so the collapsed post-wipe mark still drives liquidation decisions during the ring warm-up. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _isDead
nodes.reachability: Death has two independent causes and a strict fallback order. FIRST, a cached-quote divergence: if `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1461) no longer equals the registry's quote for the current generation, the engine declares itself dead without consulting the hook at all - this is what makes the book force-closeable after a live rotation. SECOND, the hook's own pool-death flag, read through a try/catch at `isDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1462) that reports NOT dead on any revert, so an unwired or reverting hook fails OPEN for trading and CLOSED for force-closing. Note the registry calls here are NOT wrapped, so a reverting registry bricks both openings and force-closes. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _takeFee
nodes.signature: function _takeFee(uint256 sent, bool longSide) internal returns (uint256 collateral)
nodes.reachability: Takes the open fee off the top of the stated amount, so collateral is net of fee at `collateral` (PerpEngine.sol:1467). Holding any genesis NFT halves it via `ogDiscountBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1466) - a balance check on the immutable `mifrens` (PerpEngine.sol:1466) collection, so it is transferable and re-usable by the same NFT across wallets. The `longSide` (PerpEngine.sol:1468) flag decides which staker class the yield slice rewards. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _checkNotional
nodes.reachability: Caps a single position's notional at a share of live depth so no one position can move price enough to create bad debt on its own exit. Called at `_checkNotional` (PerpEngine.sol:871) and `_checkNotional` (PerpEngine.sol:900). If depth reads 0 the product is 0 and every non-zero notional reverts. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _book
nodes.signature: function _book(address trader, bool isLong, uint256 collateral, uint256 size, uint256 principal, uint8 leverage) internal returns (uint256 id)
nodes.reachability: The only place a position is created. It snapshots `fundingIndex` (PerpEngine.sol:1481) as the position's funding baseline and truncates collateral into a uint128 at `collateral` (PerpEngine.sol:1480). The hard book cap at `MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS` (PerpEngine.sol:1477) is a constant, not a setting, because it underwrites the one-call drain guarantee of `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:1082).

nodes.name: _removeOpen
nodes.reachability: O(1) swap-and-pop removal from the enumerable open set, called at `_removeOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:1283). It no-ops on an id not in the set at `idx` (PerpEngine.sol:1488). Its swap semantics are what the sweep cursor at `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1024) and the drain loop at `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1083) both depend on.

nodes.name: _ethToToken
nodes.reachability: Sizes a short's borrow at SPOT: the token to sell at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:901) and the token-side OI cap at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:908). The conversion body is now a delegatecall into `ethToToken` (PerpSwapLib.sol:96).
observations: Unlike the liquidation path this uses spot and not the mark, so the borrow size — and therefore the OI cap comparison at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:908) — moves with an in-block price push. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _routeFee
nodes.value: pays the dividend and treasury through `_payOut` (line 1525)
nodes.reachability: Splits every routed fee. With a vault wired, the LP slice and the insurance slice are carved FIRST and stay inside the engine as counters - `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1514) for long-attributed fees, the segregated `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1516) plus its monotonic marker `tokYieldCumulative` (PerpEngine.sol:1517) for short-attributed ones, and `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1519) for both. Only the remainder leaves the contract, split by `divShareBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1523) between dividend and treasury and pushed through the non-reverting `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1525). Both recipients are owner-settable at `dividend` (PerpEngine.sol:1950), and a zero address silently forfeits that leg at `dividend` (PerpEngine.sol:1525). DERIVED.

nodes.name: _sendEth
nodes.reachability: A one-line alias kept for its callers' readability; it is the REVERTING push, so a vault withdrawal or an insurance skim to a recipient that rejects the transfer fails the whole call rather than crediting an IOU. Reached from `_sendEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1869), the tail both quote-side vault pulls share, and from `_sendEth` (PerpEngine.sol:2017).

nodes.name: _payOut
nodes.value: pushes `amount` (line 1543) of the quote to `to` through `_tryPush`, and books an IOU when that fails
nodes.reachability: The NON-reverting push used for every recipient an attacker can choose: the trader and keeper at `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1350), (PerpEngine.sol:1364) and (PerpEngine.sol:1366), and the fee sinks at `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1525) and (PerpEngine.sol:1526). On failure it credits `payoutOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1544) instead of reverting, which is what keeps one hostile trader from making `forceCloseAllDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1072) unsatisfiable. The transport and the hostile-recipient handling now live in `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1563), and each credit also raises the aggregate `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1544) that a quote adoption reads.
observations: The credit is `unchecked` at `payoutOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1544); both counters are quote-denominated and move together, so `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1544) stays the exact sum of the mapping unless an entry is retired. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _tryPush
nodes.signature: function _tryPush(address to, uint256 amount, bool capped) private returns (bool ok)
nodes.value: sends native to `to` (line 1565) with a 30k budget when `capped`, or with all remaining gas at `to` (line 1566); on an ERC20 book transfers the quote via `tryTransfer` (line 1568)
nodes.reachability: The one push that reports instead of reverting, shared by the three callers that must survive a hostile recipient: the rotation sweep at `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1228), the settlement payout at `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1543) and the escape hatch at `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1623). `capped` is true for the first two and false for the third, so only the last-chance retry forwards all gas.
observations: The gas cap is applied ONLY on the native branch (`gas` (PerpEngine.sol:1565)); the ERC20 branch at `tryTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1568) forwards all remaining gas to the token, so on an ERC20 book a recipient hook inside a callback-bearing token is not budget-bounded. The doc block above it describes `capped` as bounding the NATIVE forward, which matches. DERIVED.

nodes.name: retirePayout
nodes.authority: owner while the engine's quote matches the generation's; ANYONE while it diverges
nodes.value: pushes the retired `amount` (line 1623) to `to` at FULL gas; the value is lost to the engine as residue if that push fails
nodes.reachability: The escape hatch for the one counter that can still refuse a quote adoption: `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1207) is checked before the sweep in `syncGeneration` (PerpEngine.sol:1098), and until this existed only the recipient's own `claimPayout` (PerpEngine.sol:1632) could clear it. Effects land before the interaction (`payoutOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1616), `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1617)), so a reentering recipient finds zero, which is why it carries no `nonReentrant`.
observations: The entry is permissionless exactly while `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1615) disagrees with the generation's quote — the same divergence the death test reads at `generationQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:1461) — so anyone can then zero any recipient's claim by pushing it at full gas; the value can only go to `to` (PerpEngine.sol:1623) or nowhere, never to the caller. The claim is retired whether or not the push succeeded, since the return of `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1623) is discarded. DERIVED.

The doc block heading calls the entry `Timelock-only` (PerpEngine.sol:1573) while the code calls `_checkOwner` (PerpEngine.sol:1615) only in the converged case; the later paragraphs of the same comment describe the permissionless branch.

nodes.name: claimPayout
nodes.signature: function claimPayout() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 amount)
nodes.authority: anyone (clears only the caller's own credit)
nodes.value: pays `amount` (line 1637) of the quote to the caller through the REVERTING push
nodes.reachability: The self-service half of the IOU introduced by `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1541). It now also decrements the aggregate `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1636) that the quote adoption reads at `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1207), so a recipient draining its own claim can unblock that adoption.
observations: It pays through `_pushQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:1637), which REVERTS on failure, so a recipient that still cannot accept the asset simply reverts here and its claim survives — the counters are only cleared on a successful transfer. DERIVED.

The push is in the quote the engine holds TODAY, and the credit was booked in whatever the quote was when the settlement failed; the guard at `payoutOwedTotal` (PerpEngine.sol:1207) exists to prevent that mismatch by refusing adoption while any credit is outstanding. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _replenishPlv
nodes.reachability: LONG bad debt. By the time it runs, `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1293) has already been credited with only the reduced repayment, so this ADDS insurance cover back into `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1644), saturating at the buffer balance. Any gap beyond the buffer is simply left as a lower PLV, i.e. socialised to ETH-side stakers.

nodes.name: _absorbPlvLoss
nodes.reachability: SHORT bad debt, the mirror case: the buy-back at `_buyExactOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1305) has already spent real balance that was never booked, so this DECREASES the counters - insurance first at `fromIns` (PerpEngine.sol:1652), then `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1655) saturating at zero so an extreme gap cannot underflow and brick the liquidation.

nodes.name: _killStats
nodes.signature: function _killStats(Position memory p, uint256 bounty) internal view returns (LiqStats memory st)
nodes.reachability: Builds the on-chain snapshot minted with the badge. Entry price is principal over size at `entry` (PerpEngine.sol:1692) and liquidation price is the triggering mark over the same size at `mark` (PerpEngine.sol:1693), both scaled by 1e18 and clamped into uint128 at `liqPrice` (PerpEngine.sol:1704); collateral and bounty clamp into uint96 at `collateralWei` (PerpEngine.sol:1698). Clamping means an out-of-range value misreports rather than reverting the liquidation.

nodes.name: _awardBadge
nodes.signature: function _awardBadge(uint256 id, address to, LiqStats memory st) internal
nodes.reachability: The liquidation trophy, reached only from the liquidation tail of `_awardBadge` (PerpEngine.sol:1360). Both encodes and both gas-metered calls moved into `tryMintBadge` (PerpSwapLib.sol:70); as an external library function it runs by delegatecall, so the collection still sees the engine as `msg.sender`. Every failure path falls through to the claimable credit at `badgesOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1722), so a liquidation is never taken down by its own reward.
observations: The gas floor is now checked twice — `gasleft` (PerpEngine.sol:1719) in the engine and again at `gasleft` (PerpSwapLib.sol:71) inside the library, which sees 63/64 of it — so the library's own floor, not the engine's, is the binding one. DERIVED.

The `collection` (PerpEngine.sol:1720) read is an un-caught typed call OUTSIDE the best-effort boundary: a hook whose `collection()` reverts reverts the whole settlement, even though the mint that follows is best-effort. DERIVED.

nodes.name: claimLiquidatorBadges
nodes.authority: anyone (burns only the caller's own credit)
nodes.reachability: Claims the IOU form of the badge. It reverts rather than burning the credit when no collection is wired at `col` (PerpEngine.sol:1737), decrements `badgesOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1738) before the mint loop, and bounds work by the caller-supplied n, which is clamped down to the owed count at `owed` (PerpEngine.sol:1732). The loop makes n TYPED external calls to a hook-chosen collection at `mintLiquidator` (PerpEngine.sol:1741), so a reverting collection reverts the whole claim and the credit survives. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _safeTransfer
nodes.signature: function _safeTransfer(address token, address to, uint256 amount) private
nodes.value: transfers `amount` (line 1744) of `token` out of the engine, reverting if the token reports failure
nodes.reachability: The REVERTING ERC20 leg: the quote push at `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:219) and the token-inventory withdrawal at `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1887). The encode/call/decode itself moved to `tryTransfer` (PerpSwapLib.sol:131) and this wrapper supplies the revert, so the same library call serves both the reverting and the reporting callers.
observations: Because it reverts, a blacklisting quote token makes `PerpVault.withdrawEth` unpayable for a blacklisted staker through `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:219); the payout paths that must not be griefed use `_tryPush` (PerpEngine.sol:1563) instead. DERIVED.

nodes.name: fundPlv
nodes.signature: function fundPlv(uint256 amount) external payable onlyOwner notNested
nodes.reachability: Owner-only, share-less donation into the ETH-side PLV: it raises `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1758) with no shares minted anywhere, so the value is permanently non-withdrawable by the donor and simply lifts the vault's share price. Community capital is meant to arrive through `deposit` (PerpVault.sol:210) instead.

nodes.name: fundPlvToken
nodes.signature: function fundPlvToken(uint256 amount) external onlyOwner notNested
nodes.value: ERC20 `transferFrom` of the generation token from the owner (line 1765)
nodes.reachability: Token-side twin of the ETH donation. The pull uses the registry's LIVE `currentToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1765) rather than the engine's armed `syncedToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1410), and the return value is NOT checked here - unlike `_pull` (PerpVault.sol:249) and `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1743) - so a token that returns false instead of reverting would credit `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1766) without moving anything. DERIVED. The pull is a direct `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1765) on the registry's current token, an address this contract does not control.

nodes.name: fundInsurance
nodes.reachability: Permissionless top-up of the bad-debt buffer, with no modifiers at all. It is the only ungated way to raise `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1772) directly; the other source is the fee carve at `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1519). DERIVED.

nodes.name: creditPerpFee
nodes.reachability: The BUY-side native fee credit. The hook selects between this and its sell-side twin by trade direction at `creditPerpFee` (CauldronHook.sol:1293). It deliberately carries no nesting guard because the hook calls it mid-unlock during the engine's own swap; the gate itself lives in the private callee at `hookAddr` (PerpEngine.sol:1823).

nodes.name: creditPerpFeeToken
nodes.reachability: The SELL-side native fee credit, selected by the hook at `creditPerpFeeToken` (CauldronHook.sol:1293). Its value lands in the segregated token-staker pot at `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1843) rather than in the PLV.

nodes.name: creditPerpFeeAsset
nodes.signature: function creditPerpFeeAsset(address asset, uint256 amount) external
nodes.value: pulls `amount` (line 1811) of the quote from the hook into the ETH-side PLV
nodes.reachability: The non-native perp-fee door: the hook approves this engine and then calls it, so a balance cannot be confused with a stray transfer. It refuses anything that is not the live `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1810) and refuses `address(0)` outright, and the shared tail `_pullIntoPlv` (PerpEngine.sol:1811) is the same body `fundFromVault` (PerpEngine.sol:1855) uses.
observations: Both sides of the trade credit the ETH-side `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1818) on this path, so on a non-native generation the token stakers' sell-side share is redistributed to the ETH side rather than reaching `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1843); the doc block above states this explicitly as a deferred gap. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _pullIntoPlv
nodes.value: receives the quote through `_pullQuote` (line 1817) and banks it as ETH-side PLV
nodes.reachability: The body `creditPerpFeeAsset` and `fundFromVault` now share byte for byte, called at `_pullIntoPlv` (PerpEngine.sol:1811) and (PerpEngine.sol:1856). Both gates are in the callers — the hook check and `onlyVault` — so this itself is ungated and must never be reachable from anywhere else.
observations: It pulls from `msg.sender` at `_pullQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:1817), so the approving party is whichever caller is gated above it; nothing here distinguishes a hook fee from a vault deposit, and both land in the same `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1818) counter with a `VaultFunded` event. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _creditPerp
nodes.value: banks the incoming native `value` (line 1839) into the ETH-side PLV or the token-side reward pot
nodes.reachability: The shared body behind the hook's two native fee selectors, `_creditPerp` (PerpEngine.sol:1780) and `_creditPerp` (PerpEngine.sol:1785). It now REFUSES while the book is non-native at `_quoteIsNative` (PerpEngine.sol:1833), so native wei can no longer inflate a counter denominated in an ERC20 quote; the non-native equivalent is `creditPerpFeeAsset` (PerpEngine.sol:1806).
observations: The refusal is a revert inside a fee delivery the hook performs mid-swap, so on an ERC20 book a hook that still picks a native selector has its fee call fail rather than mis-credit. DERIVED.
`tokYieldCumulative` (PerpEngine.sol:1844) is advanced only on the token side, and it is the monotonic marker the vault folds into its per-token-share accumulator. DERIVED.

nodes.name: fundFromVault
nodes.signature: function fundFromVault(uint256 amount) external payable onlyVault
nodes.value: receives a depositor's stake through the shared `_pullIntoPlv` (line 1856)
nodes.reachability: How `PerpVault.deposit` moves working capital into the engine. The whole body is now the shared tail at `_pullIntoPlv` (PerpEngine.sol:1816), so a vault deposit and a hook asset fee are pulled and banked by identical code.
observations: It carries no `notNested` and no `nonReentrant`: the deposit direction only adds to `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1818) and touches no pool, matching the pattern of the other pull-side funders. DERIVED.

nodes.name: withdrawPlvTo
nodes.signature: function withdrawPlvTo(uint256 amount, address to) external onlyVault notNested nonReentrant
nodes.value: pays `amount` (line 1863) of the quote to `to` through the shared vault tail
nodes.reachability: The withdrawal leg the vault uses for `withdrawEth` and `claimPendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:313). It refuses to pay more than free `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1862) — lent ETH returns only as positions close — and the counter is debited BEFORE the single external send now factored into `_vaultPaid` (PerpEngine.sol:1868), preserving the original effects-then-interaction order.
observations: `_vaultPaid` (PerpEngine.sol:1863) sends through the REVERTING push, so a staker whose address cannot accept the quote fails the whole withdrawal rather than being credited an IOU. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _vaultPaid
nodes.value: sends `amount` (line 1869) of the quote to `to` and emits the withdrawal event
nodes.reachability: The tail the two quote-side vault pulls share: `_vaultPaid` (PerpEngine.sol:1863) after `plv` is debited and `_vaultPaid` (PerpEngine.sol:1875) after `tokYieldEth` is debited. Kept after the debit so both callers keep the effects-then-interaction order they had when the send was inline.
observations: Both call sites emit `VaultWithdrawn` (PerpEngine.sol:1869) with the isEth flag hard-coded true, so a token-side yield withdrawal is logged with the same flag as an ETH-side principal withdrawal. DERIVED.

nodes.name: withdrawTokYieldTo
nodes.signature: function withdrawTokYieldTo(uint256 amount, address to) external onlyVault notNested nonReentrant
nodes.value: pays `amount` (line 1875) of the quote out of the segregated token-side pot
nodes.reachability: How a token staker's short-attributed reward leaves the engine; it can never touch `plv`, only `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1874). Shares the post-debit send with `withdrawPlvTo` through `_vaultPaid` (PerpEngine.sol:1868).
observations: The pot is zeroed wholesale by the rotation sweep at `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1219), so a claim that is not drained before a quote adoption is swept to the treasury in the OLD asset; the adoption only proceeds once the vault reports no stakers at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1208). DERIVED.

nodes.name: fundTokenFromVault
nodes.value: ERC20 `transferFrom` of the generation token from the vault (line 1879)
nodes.reachability: The token-side deposit leg, called at `fundTokenFromVault` (PerpVault.sol:388) after the vault has pulled from the depositor and approved this engine. Like the owner-funded twin it does not check the transfer's return value at `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1879). DERIVED. The pull is a direct `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1879) on the registry's current token, an address this contract does not control.

nodes.name: withdrawPlvTokenTo
nodes.signature: function withdrawPlvTokenTo(uint256 amount, address to) external onlyVault notNested nonReentrant
nodes.value: ERC20 transfer of the generation token to `to` via `_safeTransfer` (line 1887)
nodes.reachability: Pays free inventory out, bounded by `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1885); lent inventory returns only as shorts buy back. Called from `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (PerpVault.sol:423) and `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (PerpVault.sol:440). It pays in the registry's CURRENT token, so after a relaunch a queued token claim is settled in the new generation's token. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setFees
nodes.signature: function setFees(uint256 _openBps, uint256 _ogDiscBps, uint256 _liqBps, uint256 _divShareBps, uint256 _keeperBps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Fee configuration behind a single owner call. Every field is range-checked at `BadParam` (PerpEngine.sol:1892): the open fee and liquidation penalty cap at 2000 bps, the rest at BPS. Changes are immediate and apply to positions already open, because `liqPenaltyBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1345) and `keeperBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1347) are read at settlement time, not at open. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setRisk
nodes.signature: function setRisk(uint256 _warmup, uint256 _ceiling, uint256 _maintBps, uint256 _maxNotBps, uint256 _maxOiBps, uint256 _fundingBpsDay) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Risk configuration. Two bounds matter beyond the obvious: the warmup floor at `MIN_TWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:1900) keeps positions from existing while the mark would still be spot, and the funding-rate ceiling at `_fundingBpsDay` (PerpEngine.sol:1917) keeps the signed step arithmetic in `fundingRateBpsPerDay` (PerpEngine.sol:806) inside int256 - an unbounded rate would either invert the funding direction or revert every path that pokes funding. Raising `maintenanceBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1918) makes already-open positions liquidatable immediately. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setTiers
nodes.signature: function setTiers(uint256[] calldata depths, uint8[] calldata levs) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Replaces both leverage tier arrays wholesale. The only invariant enforced is the length relation at `levs` (PerpEngine.sol:1933), which is exactly what `tierLeverage` (PerpEngine.sol:771) needs to index i+1 safely; the depths themselves are not required to be sorted, and the loop takes the LAST matching tier rather than the largest. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setRouting
nodes.signature: function setRouting(address _dividend, address _treasury, address _nftBeneficiary, address _markSource) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: One setter for all four outbound addresses, folded together for size headroom. `markSource` (PerpEngine.sol:1953) is the most consequential: it replaces the tick every mark, funding and liquidation decision is built from, via `_currentTick` (PerpEngine.sol:607). Setting it to zero restores the primary-pool tick, and a source that reverts or returns a malformed answer also degrades to that, so the failure mode is soft. There is no timelock or validation on any of the four. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setGuards
nodes.signature: function setGuards(uint32 _twapWindow, uint256 _maxLiqBps, uint256 _maxFundingBps) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: The three hardening knobs, all range-checked at `BadParam` (PerpEngine.sol:1957): the averaging window between `MIN_TWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:1957) and two hours, and both bps caps at BPS. `twapWindow` (PerpEngine.sol:1958) directly trades manipulation resistance against mark lag, and is read on every `twapWindow` (PerpEngine.sol:711).

nodes.name: setVault
nodes.reachability: Rotates the role that controls the working-capital surface. The drain guard asks the OUTGOING vault whether anyone still owns value, at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1978), rather than testing engine balances - so unownable residue cannot latch the guard permanently. Note the call is typed and un-caught, so the incumbent vault can block its own replacement by reverting; and while `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:1978) is zero the guard is skipped entirely.
observations: comment at `PLV` (PerpEngine.sol:1964) says a wired vault may only be re-pointed while the PLV is empty on all three counters; the code at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1978) instead asks the vault whether it has stakers, and a later note at `residues` (PerpEngine.sol:1970) explains why the balance test was replaced.

nodes.name: setVaultSplit
nodes.reachability: Sets how much of every routed fee is retained inside the engine instead of leaving to dividend and treasury. The only check is that the pair sums to at most BPS at `_yieldBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1984), so the owner can route 100 percent of fees to LP yield and insurance, or 0 percent. Both are read on every fee at `vaultYieldBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1506). DERIVED.

nodes.name: setVaultLimits
nodes.reachability: Utilization ceiling plus the insurance circuit breaker. Both only bite while a vault is wired, because the checks sit inside the `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:866) branch of the open paths. `insuranceFloor` (PerpEngine.sol:1991) has no upper bound, so a large value pauses opens indefinitely; it is also the configured half of the skim protection at `floorQ` (PerpEngine.sol:2013), where it is first scaled into quote units. DERIVED.

nodes.name: setMinCollateral
nodes.reachability: The anti-dust floor, capped at one ether at `_minCollateral` (PerpEngine.sol:1995). The value is written in wei and re-expressed in the live quote's units by `_q` (PerpEngine.sol:860) before the comparison, which is against collateral NET of the open fee, so the effective minimum deposit is higher than the configured number by the fee. DERIVED.

nodes.name: skimInsurance
nodes.signature: function skimInsurance(uint256 amount, address to) external onlyOwner
nodes.value: sends `amount` (line 2017) of the quote to `to` through the REVERTING push
nodes.reachability: The only way value leaves the insurance buffer other than covering bad debt. It protects the GREATER of the configured floor and a live-OI-scaled minimum at `protect` (PerpEngine.sol:2014), and the configured half is now rescaled into quote units by `_q` (PerpEngine.sol:2013) first — previously an 18-decimal constant was compared against a possibly 6-decimal balance. `plv` and `plvToken` are untouched.
observations: `riskMin` (PerpEngine.sol:2012) values short OI at SPOT through `_quoteEth`, not at the mark, so the protected minimum moves with an in-block price push while the configured floor does not. DERIVED.

The comment at `insuranceFloor` (PerpEngine.sol:2003) says the floor 'defaults to 0 and is never set by the deploy script', while the comment at `INSURANCE_FLOOR_WEI` (PerpEngine.sol:1193) says the deploy script arms 0.05 ether; the code reads only the stored value at `floorQ` (PerpEngine.sol:2013).

nodes.name: positionHealth
nodes.signature: function positionHealth(uint256 id) external view returns ( bool isLong, uint256 markValueEth, uint256 debtOrBackingEth, bool liquidatable )
nodes.reachability: Frontend snapshot of one position: mark value, the figure it is compared against (debt for a long, backing for a short, per `debtOrBackingEth` (PerpEngine.sol:2036)), and the same liquidation verdict the engine itself uses at `_underwater` (PerpEngine.sol:2037). Returns all-zero for a closed id at `trader` (PerpEngine.sol:2033).

A bare payable fallback with no accounting. Native value can therefore enter the engine without touching `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:319), `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:223) or `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:326) - which is required, because pool settlement returns native change to the contract during a swap, but it also means a direct send is an unattributed donation that no counter tracks. DERIVED.

nodes.name: renounceOwnership
nodes.reachability: Neutralises the {Ownable} entry on the contract whose entire owner surface IS the mark configuration: `setPrimary` (PerpMarkSource.sol:115), `addPool` (PerpMarkSource.sol:126) and `removePool` (PerpMarkSource.sol:147). The engine reads this source through a fail-soft staticcall, so a frozen configuration would keep answering with stale pools rather than degrading. DERIVED.
observations: The engine drops its own pointer to a mark source when it adopts a new quote at `markSource` (PerpEngine.sol:1241), so a stale-but-armed source is escapable from the engine side even though this contract's own configuration would be frozen. DERIVED.

nodes.reachability: Runs once at deploy. It pins the pool manager and hands ownership to `_owner` (PerpMarkSource.sol:108) through the base constructor; `armed` (PerpMarkSource.sol:72) stays false, so `armed` (PerpMarkSource.sol:174) returns 0 until a primary is set. A zero tick read by an armed engine would be a real price, but the engine only reaches this contract once an owner has wired it at `markSource` (PerpEngine.sol:1953). DERIVED.

nodes.name: setPrimary
nodes.signature: function setPrimary(PoolKey calldata key) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: The per-relaunch re-point. Setting a primary also CLEARS the sibling set at `pools` (PerpMarkSource.sol:118), because a new generation's pools have nothing to do with the old one's. There is no check that the key names a pool that exists or that its currencies match the engine's `_key` (PerpEngine.sol:533), so a mis-set primary silently becomes the mark the engine liquidates against. DERIVED.

nodes.name: addPool
nodes.signature: function addPool(PoolKey calldata key) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Adds a sibling whose depth counts toward the mark. Four refusals: not armed at `armed` (PerpMarkSource.sol:127); the cap of `MAX_POOLS` (PerpMarkSource.sol:128); a currency pair that differs from the primary's in either slot at `WrongPair` (PerpMarkSource.sol:132) - the check that keeps a cross-quote oracle off the liquidation path; and duplicates, both against the primary at `primary` (PerpMarkSource.sol:135) and against the existing set in the loop at `pools` (PerpMarkSource.sol:138). Fee tier and tick spacing are free to differ, which is the same-quote depth-splitting case this exists for.

nodes.name: removePool
nodes.signature: function removePool(PoolKey calldata key) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Swap-and-pop removal of a sibling; reverts `NotFound` (PerpMarkSource.sol:158) if the key is not in the set. The primary is not in `pools` (PerpMarkSource.sol:149) and so can never be removed - only replaced through `setPrimary` (PerpMarkSource.sol:115). Removing narrows what the mark averages, which is why it is documented as safe at any time.

nodes.name: poolCount
nodes.reachability: Size of the sibling set, excluding the primary. The only external reader of the set's cardinality; the engine never calls it, since `weightedTick` (PerpMarkSource.sol:173) takes no arguments precisely so the engine need not know the pool count. DERIVED.

nodes.name: weightedTick
nodes.signature: function weightedTick() external view returns (int24 tick)
nodes.reachability: The engine's mark source, reached only through the hand-rolled staticcall at `staticcall` (PerpEngine.sol:615). Fallback order, most to least specific: (1) not armed - return 0 at `armed` (PerpMarkSource.sol:174); (2) no siblings - return the primary's tick at `primaryTick` (PerpMarkSource.sol:180); (3) no in-range liquidity anywhere - return the primary's tick at `totalL` (PerpMarkSource.sol:200); (4) otherwise the liquidity-weighted average at `acc` (PerpMarkSource.sol:201). Each sibling with zero in-range depth is skipped at `l` (PerpMarkSource.sol:191), so a drained pool contributes no weight. The primary is weighted even when its own liquidity is zero, since its tick seeds `acc` (PerpMarkSource.sol:186) before the loop. Note case (1): an armed-false source returns tick 0, which the engine accepts as a valid answer. DERIVED.
observations: comment at `generationQuote` (PerpMarkSource.sol:18) says the engine's `_sqrtP` reads slot0 of the one pool built from the registry's generation quote; the code at `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:534) builds that key from the engine's own CACHED quote storage slot, which `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1245) is the only writer of.

nodes.name: ethShareOf
nodes.signature: function ethShareOf(address who) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only; the oracle calls it on the immutable `perpVault`)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only. Called at `ethShareOf` (PerpStakerOracle.sol:30); the implementation is the public mapping getter `ethShareOf` (PerpVault.sol:106). Because it reads LIVE shares, a wallet that has fully queued its exit reads zero here even though `pendingEthOf` (PerpVault.sol:108) still owes it. DERIVED.

nodes.name: tokShareOf
nodes.signature: function tokShareOf(address who) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only; the oracle calls it on the immutable `perpVault`)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only. Called at `tokShareOf` (PerpStakerOracle.sol:30); the implementation is the public mapping getter `tokShareOf` (PerpVault.sol:112).

Pins the vault it reads. There is no validation that `_perpVault` (PerpStakerOracle.sol:24) is a PerpVault, and the address is immutable, so a mis-wired deploy is replaced by pointing the consumer at a new oracle rather than by fixing this one. DERIVED.

nodes.name: isInstant
nodes.signature: function isInstant(address who) external view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: A pure read used by the migration vesting contract to decide whether a wallet gets its allocation at once. True when the wallet holds a live share on either side at `ethShareOf` (PerpStakerOracle.sol:30). Both calls are typed and un-caught, so a reverting vault makes every membership test revert; and the test is instantaneous, so one block of staked shares is enough to qualify. DERIVED.

nodes.name: unitOf
nodes.signature: function unitOf(address q) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine.syncGeneration)
nodes.reachability: Called once, on the cold quote-adoption path at `unitOf` (PerpEngine.sol:1243), to set the scaling factor `_q` (PerpEngine.sol:568) applies to every wei-written threshold. Defensive by construction: native returns 1e18 at `q` (PerpSwapLib.sol:38), and a failed call, a short return or an answer above 36 decimals also returns 1e18 at `d` (PerpSwapLib.sol:42).
observations: Falling back to 1e18 for a token whose `decimals()` reverts means the thresholds stay 18-decimal for a quote that may not be, so a misbehaving token fails toward the pre-scaling behaviour rather than toward zero. DERIVED.
It is a `staticcall`, so the read cannot re-enter the adoption it runs inside. DERIVED.

nodes.name: sqrtPriceAtTick
nodes.signature: function sqrtPriceAtTick(int24 t) external pure returns (uint160)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine.markSqrtPriceX96)
nodes.reachability: The tick-to-price conversion behind the liquidation mark, reached at `sqrtPriceAtTick` (PerpEngine.sol:756). Moved out of the engine because `TickMath` is an internal library whose body was being inlined at the EIP-170 ceiling; pure, one value argument, same result.
observations: `getSqrtPriceAtTick` (PerpSwapLib.sol:53) reverts on a tick outside TickMath's bounds, and the caller does not wrap it, so an out-of-range averaged tick would revert `markSqrtPriceX96` rather than fall back to spot. DERIVED.

nodes.name: tryMintBadge
nodes.signature: function tryMintBadge(address col, address to, LiqStats memory st) external returns (bool ok)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine._awardBadge)
nodes.reachability: The best-effort Liquidatoor mint, reached from the liquidation tail at `tryMintBadge` (PerpEngine.sol:1720). It tries the stats-bearing selector first and falls back to the pre-stats `mintLiquidator` (PerpSwapLib.sol:80) for an older collection; both calls are gas-metered and neither can revert the liquidation, because failure is REPORTED and the caller credits `badgesOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1722) instead. As an external library function it runs by delegatecall, so the collection still sees the engine as `msg.sender`.
observations: The code-length check at `col` (PerpSwapLib.sol:71) is what stops a call to an address with no code from reporting a successful mint. DERIVED.

Its own gas floor is checked against `gasleft` (PerpSwapLib.sol:71), which inside the delegatecall is 63/64 of the engine's, so this floor and not the engine's check at `gasleft` (PerpEngine.sol:1719) is the binding one. DERIVED.

nodes.name: quoteAt
nodes.signature: function quoteAt(uint256 size, uint256 sp) external pure returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine._quoteAt)
nodes.reachability: token-size-to-quote-value at a given sqrtPrice, reached at `quoteAt` (PerpEngine.sol:784) and therefore from both the spot and the mark valuations. Here because `FullMath.mulDiv` is an internal library that the engine was inlining six times at the EIP-170 ceiling.
observations: Both `mulDiv` (PerpSwapLib.sol:92) rounds truncate, so the value is understated by at most a wei. A zero `sp` (PerpSwapLib.sol:92) divides by zero and reverts, which is the uninitialised-pool case the engine special-cases only at `sp` (PerpEngine.sol:762). DERIVED.

nodes.name: ethToToken
nodes.signature: function ethToToken(uint256 eth, uint256 sp) external pure returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine._ethToToken)
nodes.reachability: quote-to-token at a given sqrtPrice, reached at `ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1497) and used to size a short's borrow and its OI cap.
observations: The inverse of `quoteAt` (PerpSwapLib.sol:91) with the same truncation, so a round trip through both does not return the original amount. DERIVED.

nodes.name: ethDepth
nodes.signature: function ethDepth(uint128 L, uint160 sp) external pure returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine.activeEthDepth)
nodes.reachability: The depth formula every risk cap is sized against, reached at `ethDepth` (PerpEngine.sol:763). Returns zero for an empty or uninitialised pool at `L` (PerpSwapLib.sol:103), which makes the caps bind at zero rather than divide by zero.
observations: Depth is computed from the pool's CURRENT liquidity and spot price, so it is an instantaneous figure; the caps built on it are therefore movable within a block by anyone who can shift the pool. DERIVED.

nodes.name: tryTransferFrom
nodes.signature: function tryTransferFrom(address token, address from, uint256 amount) external returns (bool)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine._pullQuote)
nodes.value: pulls `amount` (line 125) of `token` from `from` into the delegatecalling engine
nodes.reachability: The checked ERC20 pull behind every quote deposit, reached at `tryTransferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:206). Because it is an external library function invoked by delegatecall, `address(this)` (PerpSwapLib.sol:125) is still the engine, which is the intended recipient. It REPORTS rather than reverts, and the caller supplies the revert.
observations: A token with no return data is accepted at `ret` (PerpSwapLib.sol:127), which is what keeps non-compliant tokens usable; a token returning false is rejected. Neither case distinguishes a fee-on-transfer token, whose received amount is smaller than `amount` (PerpSwapLib.sol:125). DERIVED.

nodes.name: tryTransfer
nodes.signature: function tryTransfer(address token, address to, uint256 amount) external returns (bool)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; callers are PerpEngine._tryPush and PerpEngine._safeTransfer)
nodes.value: sends `amount` (line 133) of `token` from the delegatecalling engine to `to`
nodes.reachability: The single checked ERC20 send for the whole engine, reached from the reporting push at `tryTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1568) and from the reverting wrapper at `tryTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1744). Returning a boolean is what lets the payout paths credit an IOU while the withdrawal paths revert.
observations: The call forwards all remaining gas, so the 30k budget the native branch applies at `gas` (PerpEngine.sol:1565) has no equivalent here. DERIVED.

nodes.name: swapLeg
nodes.signature: function swapLeg( IPoolManager poolManager, PoolKey memory key, Req memory r, bool quoteIsCurrency0, bytes memory hookData ) external returns (uint256 spent, uint256 got)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine._swapBody)
nodes.value: settles the pay leg through `_settle` (line 199) and receives the other leg through `take` (line 200)
nodes.reachability: An `external` library function, so Solidity deploys it separately and the engine reaches it by DELEGATECALL from `swapLeg` (PerpEngine.sol:1414); it therefore runs in the engine's context - `address(this)` is the engine, settled value leaves the engine's balance and taken currency lands on the engine. It holds no storage of its own. Orientation is PASSED IN rather than re-derived: `quoteIsCurrency0` (PerpSwapLib.sol:169) decides which delta is which, and the swap direction is `z` (PerpSwapLib.sol:175), the XNOR of intent and orientation. The price limit follows the resulting direction at `limit` (PerpSwapLib.sol:176) and is the extreme tick either way, i.e. there is NO slippage bound inside the library - bounds are enforced by the engine's own minOut checks. The specified amount is signed at `spec` (PerpSwapLib.sol:181): positive for an exact-out buy, negative otherwise. Deltas are read from the pool at `quoteAmt` (PerpSwapLib.sol:193) and `tokAmt` (PerpSwapLib.sol:194), the owed side is settled and the owed-to-us side is taken at `got` (PerpSwapLib.sol:200).

nodes.name: _settle
nodes.signature: function _settle(IPoolManager poolManager, Currency c, uint256 amount) private
nodes.value: sends native to the pool manager via `settle` (line 214); ERC20 transfer of the currency to the pool manager via `transfer` (line 222)
nodes.reachability: The pay leg, in the two shapes v4 accepts. Native settles with attached value at `settle` (PerpSwapLib.sol:214) - value that comes out of the ENGINE's balance because this runs under delegatecall. An ERC20 settles by sync, transfer, settle at `sync` (PerpSwapLib.sol:216), and the transfer's return is decoded at `ok` (PerpSwapLib.sol:224) so a false-returning token fails here with a clear reason rather than surfacing later as the user's swap reverting on a non-zero delta. A zero amount short-circuits at `amount` (PerpSwapLib.sol:212).

nodes.name: migrateInventory
nodes.signature: function migrateInventory(address registry, address oldToken, uint256 fromGen) external returns (uint256 migratedIn)
nodes.authority: engine (linked library; the only caller is PerpEngine.syncGeneration)
nodes.value: burns the engine's dead-generation balance through the registry and receives the live token 1:1
nodes.reachability: Best-effort inventory migration, reached at `migrateInventory` (PerpEngine.sol:1118) before the token side is re-pointed. It uses the capacity-aware `claimByBurnUpTo` (PerpSwapLib.sol:256) by raw signature and a low-level call, so a registry without that facet — or a thin reserve — returns zero instead of reverting the sync.
observations: A shortfall is now announced by `InventoryMigrationShortfall` (PerpSwapLib.sol:274), carrying the raw revert data when the claim reverted and empty bytes when it merely came up short; emitted from a delegatecalled library, so the log carries the engine's address. The caller separately books the same shortfall against the old token at `strandedToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1135). DERIVED.

A registry that returns fewer than 32 bytes leaves `migratedIn` (PerpSwapLib.sol:258) at zero even if it burned something, which would double-count the stranded amount; the burn and the accounting are not atomic from this library's point of view. DERIVED.

DERIVED.

Runs once at deploy. Both counterparties are immutable, so a vault is bound to one engine forever - re-pointing happens on the ENGINE side at `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:1979), not here. There is no owner and no admin function anywhere in this contract: every entrypoint is permissionless and acts only on the caller's own position. DERIVED.

nodes.name: hasStakers
nodes.reachability: The replacement test the engine's vault-rotation guard calls at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1978). It ORs all four ownership counters in one expression at `pendingTok` (PerpVault.sol:168), so it answers `is anyone owed anything` rather than `is any engine counter non-zero` - which is what stops unownable residue (orphaned short-side yield, one-wei rounding dust) from latching the guard permanently.

nodes.name: hasQuoteStake
nodes.reachability: Answers whether the QUOTE-denominated side still holds anyone's value — live shares or an unclaimed queued exit — deliberately excluding the token side, whose counts a quote rotation does not redenominate. Declared for the engine at `hasQuoteStake` (PerpEngine.sol:48) and implemented here.
observations: The engine's adoption guard calls the broader `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1208), not this, so the comments at `hasQuoteStake` (PerpVault.sol:88) and (PerpVault.sol:101) that say the engine asks this one describe an intention the code does not carry out; the only callers in the tree are tests.

nodes.name: assetsEth
nodes.reachability: The asset base live shares are priced against: the engine's whole ETH-side book MINUS the queued-exit claims, saturating at zero at `pendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:187). Note it uses `totalEth` (PerpVault.sol:186), which counts capital lent to open longs, so the share price includes not-yet-returned principal.

nodes.name: assetsTok
nodes.reachability: Token-side mirror of `assetsEth` (PerpVault.sol:185): the engine's whole token book minus queued token exits, saturating at zero at `pendingTok` (PerpVault.sol:192).

nodes.name: deposit
nodes.signature: function deposit(uint256 amount) public payable nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares)
nodes.value: receives native asserted against `value` (line 218); pulls the ERC20 quote through `_pull` (line 221); forwards it to the engine at `fundFromVault` (line 229)
nodes.reachability: The ETH-side entry. Denomination is decided per call by `_engineQuote` (PerpVault.sol:216), and the two branches are mutually exclusive: native requires value to equal the stated amount, ERC20 requires no value at all at `value` (PerpVault.sol:220). Shares are priced BEFORE the funds reach the engine, so `assetsEth` (PerpVault.sol:225) is the pre-deposit base; the virtual `OFFSET` (PerpVault.sol:225) plus the +1 denominator is the inflation-attack guard. Effects (share mint) precede the single external interaction at `fundFromVault` (PerpVault.sol:229), which is also the only place value leaves this contract on this path.

nodes.name: depositEth
nodes.value: receives native and forwards the whole `msg` value (line 236)
nodes.reachability: Native-only convenience that forwards the whole message value. On an ERC20-quoted brew it necessarily fails: the inner branch demands zero value at `value` (PerpVault.sol:220) while this passes `msg.value` (PerpVault.sol:236) as the amount, and a zero amount reverts at `amount` (PerpVault.sol:211). DERIVED.

nodes.name: _engineQuote
nodes.reachability: Deliberately defensive: a raw staticcall by signature string at `quote` (PerpVault.sol:241) rather than a typed interface call, so an engine that predates multi-quote and has no such function returns no data and is treated as NATIVE at `address` (PerpVault.sol:243) instead of reverting the deposit. A short return is also treated as native at `ret` (PerpVault.sol:243). DERIVED.

nodes.name: _pull
nodes.signature: function _pull(address token, address from, uint256 amount) private
nodes.value: ERC20 pull of the depositor's balance into this vault by `transferFrom` (line 251)
nodes.reachability: Checked pull: an empty return or a decoded true is accepted, anything else reverts at `ZeroAmount` (PerpVault.sol:253) - without which shares would be minted for a deposit that never moved. Used for the ERC20-quote branch at `_pull` (PerpVault.sol:221) and for every token-side deposit at `_pull` (PerpVault.sol:386).

nodes.name: _approve
nodes.signature: function _approve(address token, address spender, uint256 amount) private
nodes.value: grants the engine an ERC20 `approve` allowance over this vault's balance (line 257)
nodes.reachability: Sets the exact allowance the engine will pull in the same transaction. Unlike `_pull` (PerpVault.sol:249) it checks only the call's success flag and NOT the returned boolean at `ok` (PerpVault.sol:258); the following engine pull would revert anyway if the allowance had not been set. It writes a fresh absolute allowance rather than incrementing, so a token that rejects a non-zero-to-non-zero approval would fail here. DERIVED.

nodes.name: withdrawEth
nodes.signature: function withdrawEth(uint256 shares) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 paid, uint256 queued)
nodes.authority: anyone (redeems only the caller's own shares)
nodes.value: pays the caller out of the engine at `withdrawPlvTo` (line 282)
nodes.reachability: Redemption is split by AVAILABILITY, not by entitlement: the owed amount is priced at the live share price at `owed` (PerpVault.sol:268), then capped by the engine's free buffer at `free` (PerpVault.sol:269) with the remainder queued at `queued` (PerpVault.sol:271). Ordering is strict CEI - shares are burned and the queue is earmarked at `pendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:279) before the single external call at `withdrawPlvTo` (PerpVault.sol:282). Queueing converts at-risk shares into a fixed nominal claim that leaves the share base; the pro-rata write-down at `_haircut` (PerpVault.sol:303) is what keeps that from being a free option.

nodes.name: _haircut
nodes.signature: function _haircut(uint256 owed, uint256 backing, uint256 claims) private pure returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: The pro-rata write-down applied to a queued claim. It is a no-op while backing covers the whole queue at `claims` (PerpVault.sol:308); otherwise every claimant is scaled by backing over claims at `backing` (PerpVault.sol:309), rounding DOWN toward the vault. It is pure, so it writes nothing itself - the callers persist the reduction at `pendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:318) and `pendingTok` (PerpVault.sol:433).

nodes.name: claimPendingEth
nodes.signature: function claimPendingEth() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 paid)
nodes.authority: anyone (pays only the caller's own queued exit)
nodes.value: pays `paid` (line 333) of the quote to the caller by pulling it out of the engine's free PLV
nodes.reachability: The drain side of the ETH exit queue. It now applies the pro-rata write-down at `_haircut` (PerpVault.sol:317) BEFORE paying, so a shortfall is shared across the whole queue rather than going to whoever claims first, and a claim written down to nothing RETURNS at `owed` (PerpVault.sol:327) instead of reverting — which is what lets `pendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:332) actually reach zero and the side be reopened in a new quote.
observations: The two write-down assignments at `pendingEthOf` (PerpVault.sol:318) survive the call only because of that return; the same line pair used to be rolled back by a revert on the next line, per the comment above it. DERIVED.

A partial payment is still possible at `free` (PerpVault.sol:329): when the engine's free PLV is short, the rest of the (already haircut) claim stays queued at `pendingEthOf` (PerpVault.sol:331), and a zero free balance reverts at `paid` (PerpVault.sol:330). DERIVED.

The invariant written at `hasQuoteStake` (PerpVault.sol:88) names this function's write-down as the second half of its enforcement, and the engine-side half is the broader stakers check rather than the quote-side one.

nodes.name: _syncTokYield
nodes.reachability: Folds newly accrued short-side yield into the per-share index. The watermark at `lastTokYieldCum` (PerpVault.sol:354) is advanced ALWAYS, including when `tokShares` (PerpVault.sol:355) is zero - so yield that accrued with nobody staked is emitted as unattributed and can never be back-paid to whoever deposits next. That orphaned value stays in the engine's segregated pot, which only ever pays attributed claims. DERIVED.

nodes.name: _settleTok
nodes.reachability: Banks a user's earned-so-far reward into their owed balance, at the OLD share count - which is why every caller runs it before touching `tokShareOf` (PerpVault.sol:361). The comparison at `tokRewardDebt` (PerpVault.sol:364) makes a baseline above the accrued figure a silent no-op rather than an underflow.

nodes.name: _resetTokDebt
nodes.reachability: Rebases the user's reward baseline to their CURRENT share count. Always paired after `_settleTok` (PerpVault.sol:360); the pair is what makes a share-count change neither forfeit nor duplicate accrued reward.

nodes.name: depositToken
nodes.signature: function depositToken(uint256 amount) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 shares)
nodes.value: pulls the generation token from the depositor at `_pull` (line 386) and hands it to the engine at `fundTokenFromVault` (line 388)
nodes.reachability: The token-side entry. Reward bookkeeping is settled at the old share count first at `_settleTok` (PerpVault.sol:379), shares are priced against the pre-deposit base at `assetsTok` (PerpVault.sol:380), and the baseline is rebased at `_resetTokDebt` (PerpVault.sol:384) before any external movement. The asset is whatever the registry currently names at `currentToken` (PerpVault.sol:378), so this is always the live generation's token. Token principal is structurally protected because a short's buy-back restores the inventory in full at `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1306).

nodes.name: claimTokYield
nodes.signature: function claimTokYield() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 paid)
nodes.authority: anyone (claims only the caller's own accrued reward)
nodes.value: pays the caller out of the engine's segregated pot at `withdrawTokYieldTo` (line 399)
nodes.reachability: Pays the short-attributed reward WITHOUT converting token principal: the stake stays staked. Effects before interaction - the owed balance is zeroed at `tokRewardOwed` (PerpVault.sol:398) before the engine call at `withdrawTokYieldTo` (PerpVault.sol:399). The reward leaves the engine through its quote-denominated push, while the pot itself was credited from native value on the native fee path at `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1843).

nodes.name: withdrawToken
nodes.signature: function withdrawToken(uint256 shares) external nonReentrant returns (uint256 paid, uint256 queued)
nodes.authority: anyone (redeems only the caller's own shares)
nodes.value: pays the caller token out of the engine at `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (line 423)
nodes.reachability: Token-side mirror of `withdrawEth` (PerpVault.sol:263), with the reward bookkeeping wrapped around it: bank at the old count at `_settleTok` (PerpVault.sol:410), burn shares, rebase at `_resetTokDebt` (PerpVault.sol:418), queue the shortfall at `pendingTok` (PerpVault.sol:420), and only then call the engine at `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (PerpVault.sol:423).

nodes.name: claimPendingToken
nodes.signature: function claimPendingToken() external nonReentrant returns (uint256 paid)
nodes.authority: anyone (claims only the caller's own queued exit)
nodes.value: pays the caller token out of the engine at `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (line 440)
nodes.reachability: Token-side twin of `claimPendingEth` (PerpVault.sol:313), with the same persisted pro-rata write-down at `pendingTokOf` (PerpVault.sol:433). The engine pays in the registry's CURRENT token at `currentToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1887), so a claim queued before a relaunch is settled in the NEW generation's token while the queued number was priced against the old inventory. DERIVED.

nodes.name: ethPosition
nodes.signature: function ethPosition(address user) external view returns (uint256 redeemable, uint256 instant, uint256 pending)
nodes.reachability: Frontend view mirroring `withdrawEth` (PerpVault.sol:263) exactly: same pricing formula at `redeemable` (PerpVault.sol:450) and the same free-buffer cap at `free` (PerpVault.sol:451), plus the caller's already-queued balance. It does NOT apply the haircut, so the pending figure it reports is the un-written-down claim.

nodes.name: tokenPosition
nodes.signature: function tokenPosition(address user) external view returns (uint256 redeemable, uint256 instant, uint256 pending)
nodes.reachability: Token-side mirror of `ethPosition` (PerpVault.sol:448), using the same formula as `assetsTok` (PerpVault.sol:411).

nodes.name: pendingTokYield
nodes.signature: function pendingTokYield(address user) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Simulates the fold plus the settle without writing. It mirrors the zero-share rule exactly - the un-folded delta is only added when `tokShares` (PerpVault.sol:470) is positive - so the view never promises unattributed yield that `_syncTokYield` (PerpVault.sol:350) would refuse to credit.
